competitors.name: National Frozen & Refrigerated Foods Association
competitors.action: NFRA reported that air fryers are now in 71% of American homes and that more than half of owners say the appliance has led them to buy more frozen foods. Despite that demand signal, only 33% of shoppers say most products they buy include air-fryer directions, identifying an immediate packaging and preparation-guidance gap for frozen brands.

trends.topic: Air-fryer adoption is increasing frozen-food purchasing and broadening usage occasions
trends.magnitude: More than half of air-fryer owners report buying more frozen food because of the appliance, rising to 67% of Millennials and 63% of Gen Z; core users over-index for breakfast and lunch by 13 points each and after-school snacks by 10 points.
trends.context: The findings were published by a frozen-food trade association, and the full study methodology is available only through NFRA's member portal. The operational signal is still specific: frozen brands can reduce preparation friction with validated air-fryer instructions and a front-of-pack cue, while testing pizza occasions beyond dinner. Real Dough should confirm product quality and food-safety directions through formal cook testing before making any package claim.

market_data.metric: Air-fryer ownership and frozen-food purchase effect
market_data.value: Air fryers are present in 71% of American homes; more than half of owners say the appliance has led them to purchase more frozen food
market_data.change: Only 33% of shoppers say most products they buy include air-fryer directions, while 45% cite on-package instructions as a top driver of increased air-fryer use

breaking.headline: Air Fryers Are Now in 71% of American Homes — and Frozen and Refrigerated Brands Are Positioned to Win
